content.text: Note: Relative potency = mg ≈ fluoxetine 40 mg/day (Hayasaka 2015)    -    — = no published RCT equivalent    -    †doxepin not corroborated on sensitivity analysis
: block reuptake of NE, 5HT, or both from the synaptic cleft back into the presynaptic nerve terminal; also block histamine1, muscarinic, & alpha1 adrenergic receptors
•Tertiary Amines: more effective, but more side effects
•Secondary Amines: less side effects; less drowsiness, somnolence, & weight gain
•anticholinergic (MC) – dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, mydriasis, blurred vision, tachycardia
•cardiovascular: dose-dependent QT prolongation, orthostatic hypotension, conduction abnormalities, tachycardia
•CNS: seizures, fine tremor, sedation, sleep alterations, activation-like state, anxiety
•weight gain, confusion, edema, rash, worsening glaucoma
: concurrent use w/ MAOIs, concurrent use w/ Methyldopa & Clonidine
: do not D/C abruptly – cholinergic rebound
